subject: highlight a small set of points among a much larger set

messages.author: de80823ab00b5d5b
messages.subject: highlight a small set of points among a much larger set
parts:
Hey Group,

I am trying to plot two sets of points using two colors. The second
set is much smaller than the first set, so when I plot them, we cannot
really see the second set among all the points. Here is an example

library("ggplot2")
N1 <- 10000
N2 <- 10
myData1 <- data.frame(x=
rnorm(N1,6,3),y=runif(N1),condition=rep("treatment",N1))
myData2 <- data.frame(x= rnorm(N2,6,3),y=runif(N2),condition=rep("control",N2))
allData <- rbind(myData1,myData2)

library(ggplot2)
p <- ggplot(allData,aes(x=x,y=y,colour=factor(condition)))
p <- p + geom_point()
p

To work around this, I used layers. But then I lose the legend
indicating what the color corresponds to.

library(ggplot2)
p <- ggplot(myData1,aes(x=x,y=y))
p <- p + geom_point(alpha=0.1)
p <- p + layer(data=myData2,mapping=aes(x=x,y=y),geom='point',colour='red')
p

Any suggestions on how to improve my plot. Thanks!

Juliet

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: highlight a small set of points among a much larger set
parts:
How about using scale size and manually defining the color? 

#adjusting size
library(ggplot2)
p <- ggplot(allData,aes(x=x,y=y,colour=factor(condition), size=factor(condition)))

p <-  p + geom_point()
p

#adding manual color
p+ scale_colour_manual(values = c("pink", "black"))


Brandon

This works, more or less ... although I think it's a bit of an
accident. Couldn't figure out the equivalent of scale_alpha_manual,
although I guess one could hack up a way to use scale_alpha_identity ...

ggplot(allData,aes(x=x,y=y,colour=factor(condition),
alpha=as.numeric(condition)))+
geom_point()+
scale_alpha_continuous(legend=FALSE)+
scale_colour_manual(value=c("black","red"))
